The video identifies several companies across three key growth themes.  
 
Data Center Theme 
The speaker lists these companies as part of the data center value chain, which includes land, infrastructure, power, cooling, and connectivity: 
 
Anant Raj: Mentioned for its involvement in land and real estate. (3:51) 
Techno Electric, E2E Networks, Cummins India, Hitachi Energy, and Sterlite Technologies: Mentioned as part of the 15-company list evaluated for their Q1 FY27 profit-after-tax (PAT) and topline growth. (5:33-6:04) 
Capital Markets & Wealth Generation Theme 
These companies are highlighted for their high PAT growth rates during Q1 FY27, driven by the increasing shift of Indian household savings into financial assets: 
 
Groww, MCX, BSE, and Nippon India AMC: Highlighted for significant profit growth. (9:12-9:20) 
Nuvama (Nama), Anand Rathi, and 361: Mentioned as examples of wealth management firms, which the speaker identifies as a potentially high-growth segment. (11:23-11:27) 
Energy Theme 
These companies are noted for significant PAT growth in Q1 FY27, benefiting from the massive capital inflow projected for the energy sector: 
 
Adani Energy Solutions, Hitachi Energy India, Oil India, Siemens, Premier Energies, Adani Power, and NTPC: Cited for their strong bottom-line growth (ranging from 53% to 130%). (14:51-15:05) 
Reliance Industries and Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC): Listed as top companies within the Nifty Energy Index. (16:23-16:25)

Excellent breakdown, and thank you especially for the point that very few listed names actually earn the majority of their revenue from data centres — that single line saves people from a lot of story-buying.
One nuance worth adding on the Budget 2026 announcement: the holiday isn't for companies that set up data centres in India. What it does is exempt foreign companies from Indian tax on income earned by serving their global customers from Indian data centres (till FY2046-47) — while services to Indian customers must still route through a taxed Indian reseller. So Indian listed players don't get a tax break; they get demand. That actually strengthens your picks-and-shovels framing: power equipment, cooling, fibre and land benefit from the capex the policy attracts, not from the exemption itself.
